text:
Fixed in my eyes remains

the vision of that wagon of wheat

that crossed, creaking and heavy,

sowing the straight road with ears of grain.


Do not expect me to laugh now!

You do not know the deep memories

in which I am absorbed!


From the depths of my soul rises

the taste of pitanga to my lips.

My brown skin still holds

some nameless fragrance of stacked wheat.


Oh, I would like to take you with me

to sleep one night in the fields,

and in your arms pass into day

beneath a tree's unruly roof!


I am the same wild girl

you brought to your side years ago.

translation.title: Wild Root
translation.editorial_note: Pitanga remains untranslated as a regional sensory anchor; the rural memory keeps its erotic and autobiographical force.
